1) Allocation rule: our standard renewal credit is applied first to baseline committed consumption; any incremental usage beyond the committed monthly allocation is billed as overage on the end-of-term invoice unless a negotiated true-up is requested.

2) Because you have remaining renewal credit from the Q2 amendment, we can apply credits to the baseline first, then bill the spike as a separate overage line on the final statement.

Proposed next steps (I can own coordination):
- Karthik (billing tax) and Marissa (invoicing) to confirm VAT/tax treatment for the overage line and produce a revised end-term statement.
- Marissa to attach payment instructions that match Redwood's wire and SEPA details and include the PO reference you provided.
- We aim to send a revised statement by EOD Thursday so your AP has time to start payment before next week.

- If CloudRipple wants the overage rounded into the same invoice (single PDF), we can include a distinct invoice line for the overage but issue it on the same end-term statement date. That keeps a single payable document while preserving the accounting separation.
- If CloudRipple prefers the overage on a separate invoice number (for internal ledgering), Marissa can issue a standalone invoice and link it via the HubSpot deal id. This is slightly slower (requires separate invoice number allocation) but is common for customers who need separate GL codes.

I recommend same-PDF approach to avoid payment delays; Marissa, can you produce a combined end-term statement with a clear overage line and include the tax breakdown?
